reasoning: Two models (qwen and deepseek) completed successful audits and found no security issues. The PKGBUILD uses standard VCS packaging practices: git+https from the declared upstream repository (github.com/roddhjav/apparmor.d), SKIP checksum (normal for VCS sources), and benign pkgver() using git describe. The apparmor.d.install script only prints warnings via echo statements with no network operations or code execution. No malicious injection patterns were detected in any reviewed files.
disagreement_analysis: No analytical disagreement exists. The three INCONCLUSIVE verdicts resulted from tool errors (403 model unavailability, 429 rate limiting, and malformed response), not security concerns. The two models that completed analysis both correctly identified the package as safe with consistent reasoning.
coverage_issues: qwen and deepseek models selected files without the src/apparmor.d-git/ prefix, causing 6 and 3 files respectively to not be reviewed (dists/docker.sh, dists/docstring.sh, share/libalpm/hooks/apparmor.hook, share/zsh/site-functions/_aa-*.zsh)
openrouter/free model had a malformed response for docker.sh, leaving it inconclusive despite the file being reviewed
thinkingmachines/inkling:free and z-ai/glm-5.2:free models failed entirely due to infrastructure errors (403 and 429)
learnings: Models need better path resolution logic: when files are in src/<pkgname>/, models should be guided to use the full path or the file selection prompt should clarify the directory structure
The audit tool should handle malformed model responses more gracefully by retrying or falling back to a simpler assessment rather than marking the entire audit inconclusive

Free-tier models have reliability issues (rate limiting, availability) that should be factored into audit planning; consider using paid models for critical audits or implementing automatic retry with fallback models
For VCS packages (-git), the audit tool should explicitly confirm that SKIP checksums are expected and not flag them as unpinned sources, reducing noise in the assessment
